“Such a result simply means that, while the jurisdiction of the Courts of Appeals is limited now, as when 106 (a) was enacted, to the review of all final orders of deportation, a change in the administrative regulations relating to the processing and determination of applications for 243 (h) relief had the incidental effect of expanding the decisional content of such orders.”

“This Courts holding that the Court of Appeals lacked jurisdiction was based on the fact that the alien did not attack the deportation order itself but instead [sought] relief not inconsistent with it. … Here, in contrast, Chadha directly attacks the deportation order itself, and the relief he seeks … is plainly inconsistent with the deportation order.”

“We have previously construed such final order language to authorize judicial review of all matters on which the validity of the final order is contingent, rather than only those determinations actually made at the hearing.”
